How to Reach Odisha
TRAVEL GUIDE
How to Reach Odisha

Odisha is well connected to major cities across India through an extensive network of air, rail, and road connectivity. The State is accessible through international and domestic airports, major railway routes, and National Highways connecting eastern, northern, western, and southern regions of the country. Travelers can conveniently reach Odisha from different parts of India and abroad for tourism, pilgrimage, business, and cultural exploration.

By Air
By Rail
By Road
By Air

Air travel is one of the fastest and most convenient ways to reach Odisha. The State is served by multiple airports, with Biju Patnaik International Airport (BBI) being the primary gateway to Odisha. Located approximately 6 kilometers from the city center, the airport offers regular domestic and international connectivity to cities such as Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and Raipur.

Other operational airports in Odisha include:

Veer Surendra Sai Airport (Domestic)

Major tourist destinations such as Puri are easily accessible from Bhubaneswar by road. Taxi, cab, and bus services are available from the airport for onward travel.

 Visitors are advised to book flight tickets in advance during peak tourism and festive seasons.

TRAVEL GUIDE
Getting Around Odisha

Getting around Odisha is convenient, comfortable, and well-connected through a modern network of public transport, intercity rail services, app-based mobility solutions, and guided tourism services.

Buses

Public bus services provide affordable and efficient connectivity across major cities and tourist destinations in Odisha.

Mo Bus

Operated by Capital Region Urban Transport, Mo Bus connects Bhubaneswar, Kataka, and Puri through modern, air-conditioned coaches equipped with digital ticketing and real-time tracking.

OSRTC Services

Odisha State Road Transport Corporation operates extensive intercity coaches connecting all major towns, cities, and popular pilgrimage sites across the State.

Trains

Rail travel is one of the fastest and most convenient ways to travel between major destinations within Odisha.

 Key railway stations include:
Bhubaneswar Railway Station
Puri Railway Station
Kataka Railway Station
Brahmapur Railway Station
Baleshwar Railway Station

Frequent train services connect major tourism and business destinations across the State.

Cabs - Taxis

App-based cab services and private taxis are widely available in major urban centers including Bhubaneswar, Kataka, and Puri.

 Popular mobility platforms include:
Odisha Yatri
Ola
Rapido

Pre-paid taxis, rental vehicles, and chauffeur-driven cars are also available for airport transfers, sightseeing, and intercity travel.

Auto Rickshaws - Bike Taxis

For quick urban travel and navigating narrow streets, auto rickshaws and bike taxis offer highly efficient local transit.

Auto Rickshaws

Auto-rickshaws are easily available for short-distance travel within all cities and major towns across Odisha. Shared auto services operate on fixed local routes.

Bike Taxi

App-based bike taxi services provide a quick and economical option for solo travelers navigating busy city traffic routes.

Guided Tours

Organized sightseeing and packages offer curated travel itineraries with local expert assistance.

OTDC Sightseeing

Organized sightseeing and tourism packages are available through Odisha Tourism Development Corporation (OTDC) and authorized tour operators.

Traveler Services

These services offer comfortable travel arrangements, curated itineraries, and local travel assistance for visitors exploring Odisha's sights.

LUXURY & HERITAGE STAYS
Where Every Palace Tells a Story

Odisha's heritage stays invite travelers to experience a side of the state that few destinations can offer. These historic palaces, forts and royal residences, many of which continue to be home to the erstwhile royal families, open a window into centuries of history, architecture and tradition.

Each property reflects the character of its region. Nestled beside rivers, amidst forests or overlooking rolling hills, these heritage homes have been thoughtfully restored to preserve their original charm while offering the comforts of a memorable stay. From elegant Victorian mansions and riverside palaces to secluded hunting lodges and historic fort residences, every destination has a story waiting to be discovered.

A stay at these heritage properties is about more than beautiful architecture. It is an opportunity to walk through grand courtyards and Durbar Halls, admire antique collections and family heirlooms, savor recipes rooted in royal kitchens, and engage with traditions that continue to thrive through the generations. Conversations with the host families, who remain custodians of these remarkable residences, add a personal dimension to every visit.

Beyond the palace gates lies another journey. Many heritage stays are located close to wildlife sanctuaries, mangrove forests, rivers, waterfalls, ancient temples, Buddhist sites, weaving villages and traditional craft clusters, making them ideal starting points for exploring the diverse landscapes and living heritage of Odisha.

Whether you are drawn by history, architecture, nature or culture, Odisha's heritage properties offer experiences that are intimate, authentic and deeply connected to the places they call home.

MUST EXPERIENCE
Signature Experiences
Royal Heritage

Explore palaces that have preserved centuries of architectural splendor, royal traditions and family legacies.

Culture & Traditions

Experience Odisha through its classical dance, regional cuisine, festivals, crafts and local customs.

Nature & Wildlife

Venture into nearby forests, rivers, wetlands and wildlife habitats that surround many of the heritage properties.

Craft & Handloom

Meet skilled artisans, visit traditional weaving centers and discover the timeless craftsmanship that defines Odisha's rich cultural identity.

Slow Travel

Enjoy peaceful walks through palace gardens, riverside landscapes, village trails and quiet countryside, where every experience unfolds at an unhurried pace.

GUIDELINES FOR RESPONSIBLE & SAFE TRAVEL

Travel Tips & Guidelines

Do’s & Don’ts
Do's & Don'ts

Guidelines for a respectful and safe journey through the beautiful land of Odisha.

Responsible Tourism
Tourist Guide
Do's
Dress Modestly: While visiting temples and religious sites, ensure your shoulders and knees are covered as a mark of respect.
Remove Footwear: Always take off your shoes before entering temples, shrines, and local homes.
Respect Local Customs: Ask for permission before taking photos of people, especially in tribal areas.
Use Dustbins: Help keep Odisha clean by disposing of waste in designated bins, especially at beaches and heritage sites.
Stay Hydrated: The climate can be humid; carry water and stay hydrated, especially during summer visits.
Try Local Cuisine: Experience authentic Odia dishes like Pakhala, Dalma, and Chhena Poda from hygienic eateries.
Carry Identification: Always keep a copy of your ID proof handy, especially when checking into hotels or booking travel.
Follow Safety Instructions: Adhere to lifeguard instructions at beaches and safety guidelines during boating or adventure activities.
Don'ts
Don't Enter Restricted Areas: Some temples, including the Jagannath Temple in Puri, restrict entry to non-Hindus. Please respect these traditions.
Don't Use Plastic: Avoid using single-use plastics at eco-sensitive zones like Chilika Lake and Similipal National Park.
Don't Touch Deities/Idols: Unless explicitly allowed, avoid touching statues and idols at religious places.
Don't Smoke/Drink Publicly: Smoking and drinking alcohol in public places, especially near religious sites, is discouraged and often prohibited.
Don't Feed Wildlife: Feeding monkeys or other wildlife at tourist spots can be dangerous and disrupt their natural diet.
Don't Engage Touts: Avoid unofficial guides and touts. Use only authorized tourist guides or services approved by Odisha Tourism.
Don't Sunbathe Nude: Public nudity is strictly prohibited on beaches and public places.
Don't Buy Endangered Souvenirs: Avoid purchasing products made from endangered species or protected wildlife.
